title: EtaleHypercoverHomotopyEqualizer
statement: For quasi-compact quasi-separated $X$, finite split étale hypercovers $U,V$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover], and two simplicial maps $a,b:U\to V$, there is an étale hypercover $K$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-hypercover], a simplicial map $c:K\to U$, and an elementary simplicial homotopy from $ca$ to $cb$. No splitting or finiteness is asserted for $K$.

proof.text: In degree n represent maps from the finite simplicial set Delta[1] times Delta[n] to V by the finite limit of V's terms indexed by its nondegenerate simplices and face relations. These limits exist in the etale site and remain limits after forgetting to schemes over X. Restriction along simplicial operators defines the endpoint path object of V. Pull its endpoint map back along (a,b) from U. Its projection c to U carries the universal simplicial homotopy between c followed by a and c followed by b. To verify the hypercover condition, the relative matching maps are restrictions from the whole prism to the endpoint simplices together with its boundary. The inclusion adds finitely many nondegenerate simplices. Finite simplex lifting makes these restrictions covering; base change preserves the covers. The singleton matching comparison identifies this covering condition with the scheme matching condition. In degree zero the relative arrow is a pullback of V_1 to V_0 times_X V_0. In each higher degree compose the relative covering arrow with the base change of U's matching cover to obtain K's absolute matching cover. The resulting K need not be finite or split; finite replacement is a separate step.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_etale_hypercover_homotopy_equalizer
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (U V : FiniteSplitEtaleHypercover X) (a b : U.Refinement V) :
    ∃ (K : SimplicialObject X.Etale) (hK : IsEtaleHypercover K)
      (c : K ⟶ U.simplicial), Nonempty (SimplicialObject.Homotopy (c ≫ a) (c ≫ b))
